title.suggested: Mace Replies to Allen's Challenge and Allen Sends His Deposit

summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican printed Jem Mace's reply to Allen, depositing $500 and offering to meet in New York. Billy Carroll then sent $500 for Allen, proposing $2,500 a side near Cincinnati on July 5, 1870.

metadata.notes: Masthead: The Missouri Republican, St. Louis, January 1, 1870. Mace's card dated New York, Dec. 27, 1869.

facts.fact: Jem Mace deposited $500 at the New York Clipper office to cover Allen's challenge, refused to meet at Pittsburgh, offered to meet in New York and pay half Allen's expenses, and proposed to stake a belt from his New York friends against Allen's

Billy Carroll, for Allen, forwarded $500 forfeit to Frank Queen of the New York Clipper, proposing to fight Mace for $2,500 a side within fifty miles of Cincinnati on July 5, 1870, for the championship of the world, any party arrested in another state to forfeit

notes: Carroll's deposit sent 'yesterday' relative to Jan 1, 1870. A short note on a Collyer-Edwards match is not about Allen.
